title: Patrick Wilson and @Grace Aki talk about the process of getting @The ...
transcript: I called Warner Brothers. I called Mark Kaufman at Warner Brothers and he said, what's your pitch? Cause. And he said, this. He goes, this. We've had 13 producers with- much more experienced producers ask for this this year. It's our most sought after property for stage to screen adaptations at Warner Brothers. This is true. And he goes, why you guys? Vampire musicals don't work. And I said, you're right. I said, I don't see it as a vampire musical. I see it as a mom who takes her two boys, uh, starting a new life. They're both going through their own crisis, trying to figure out who they are. And yes, the older one falls in with the wrong crowd. Or the right crowd, depending on who you like. Um, and they happen to be vampires. I said, so unlike any of those other vampire musicals that didn't work, and we could debate that or. Or not, they weren't the centre of the emotional story. We raised money, hired Michael Arden. What made you believe, like, you are the right fit for the story? Yeah. What's funny is we hired him before parade, maybe at the beginning. I mean, all the other shows that he's done. Cause this is like five years ago. So. What really pushed us over the edge was Christmas Carol. That showed me the real sort of horror purist. Like, okay, can we. Can we at least make it spooky on stage? Like, do You get the tone? Do you understand what we wanted to do? We want to produce a show where theatre is going, not where it's been. What about this story sang to you? Because obviously, yeah, you could have just been like, this could be great as a play, like you mentioned, like the Christmas Carol. Sure. What about Musically? The movie is so musical. All of Joel Schumacher’s movies are incredibly musical. The score of this movie is fantastic. That being said, the needs of a musical, as you know, are much different than what you need for a film, you know, so there was never really a world where we were gonna use all the songs from the movie. It was just about finding the right sound to support that. But it. It. The movie felt musical to me. I mean, you do you. When you look for property, you're like, can it sing? Does it sing? And like, even if you like the movie, it may not sing to me, this movie. Just saying, you could see the song breaks, you could see where this stuff was gonna happen. And me as the guy who's to go between. Between Arden and the studio, like, I'm. I'm. My whole job was to try to really honour the legacy, but then really give my director the tools to go make something really daring. Cause you don't wanna just handicap him and say, you gotta do this, gotta do that, You're certainly not gonna do that to Michael Arden. Cause we wanted to create a show that we loved as kids. You know, I came up in the 80s with like phantom and Les Mis like my first job was Miss Saigon. Like, I love a big musical, kinda like I love a big movie. Like, so I wanted to, you know, if we could pull it off, I wanted to create an experience that you went back and we're like, oh my god, look at this show. In this world where we all love an escape, and certainly for in a Broadway theatre, I want you to go and enjoy a big old Broadway show that is gonna hopefully entertain you and give you a thrill. Also maybe move you in places that you didn't think you'd be moved. Um, and ultimately maybe find out who you belong to.
classificationReason: This is an interview with Patrick Wilson and Grace Aki about the development and origin of The Lost Boys musical (vampire story, mom + two sons, director Michael Arden, Warner Brothers rights). The video creator is not sharing a personal opinion on seeing the stage production — it is promotional/behind-the-scenes commentary.
